find: both are marked in points. A student absent for a quiz or the test takes it within two school days of returning. Quiz corrections done in class earn back half of the points lost.
why: A make-up deadline and a half-credit corrections rule the brief never set (reader, strictS59).

find: pieces are marked in points. A student absent for a quiz or the test takes it within two school days of returning. Quiz corrections done in class earn back half of the points lost. Say that quiz and test dates are announced in class, and do not describe the format beyond what is on the screen.
replace: pieces are marked in points. Say that quiz and test dates are announced in class.
why: Same invented policy in the speaker notes, plus a writer's rule passed to the teacher.

find: announced in class. Do not describe the quiz or test format beyond what is on the screen.

find: so you must add before you write a part-to-whole ratio.
replace: so add the parts when a story gives only the parts; when it states the total, such as 30 students in a class, use that total as the second term.
why: As written it gives 6:21 on the exit ticket and a whole of 23 on the Sort sheet.

find: The idea behind all three is that you do the same thing to both terms.
replace: The idea behind all three is that you multiply or divide both terms by the same number, never add the same amount to both.
why: "The same thing to both terms" is the additive slip (3:2 to 5:4) the lesson refutes.

find: Keep scoops in the first column and water in the second
replace: Keep scoops in the scoops column and water in the water column
why: The table's first column is Batches.

find: Find the number that takes the first term of one ratio to the first term of the other. Then check that the same number takes the second term to the second term.
replace: Find the number that takes a term of one ratio to the matching term of the other (first to first, or second to second). Then check that the same number works for the other pair of terms.
why: The guide's own 5:4 example starts from the second terms; no whole number takes 3 to 5.

find: What takes one first term to the other?
replace: What number takes one first term to the other? If none is a whole number, start with the second terms and check the first.
why: Students alone on 5:4 vs 3:2 reach a dead end at 3 → 5.

find: adding the first column again and again
replace: adding the first row again and again
why: The first column is Batches; the rows are the ratios.
